title: Opposites

parent.learn: Opposites are pairs of words that mean very different things: hot–cold, up–down.
parent.why: Learning words in pairs teaches both meanings at once, and helps compare things (“the tea is hot, the ice is cold”).

parent.learn: Act them out: open and close the door, walk fast and slow.
parent.why: Doing the action makes the meaning clear without any explanation.

parent.learn: Use them to describe things around the house.
parent.why: Describing (“the bag is full, the box is empty”) builds vocabulary for speaking and, later, writing.

ask: What is the opposite of big? Of happy?
Show me fast walking. Now slow walking.
Open your hand. Now close it.
Is the cup full or empty?
Is the light on or off?
Push the chair. Now pull it.
